purpose: Resolve the apparent contradiction between a positive Palmer colony-size reproductive-performance result and a null same-denominator ratio sensitivity by separating denominator source from statistical estimand.

chick_census.role: January chick counts plus legacy num_breeding_pairs field

common_frame.require: adult November pairs >0, legacy chick-table pairs >0, chicks >=0

denominator_comparison.model: conditional multinomial log-linear allocation of total island-season chicks
denominator_comparison.size_effect: probability proportional to pairs_i * exp(beta * z(log1p pairs_i))
denominator_comparison.reason: Count-space conditioning avoids the algebraic coupling created by regressing chicks/pairs directly on the same pair denominator.

ratio_diagnostic.summary: equal-weight mean within-island-season OLS slopes on the same common frame

outputs: per-island conditional beta under each denominator source
leave-one-island-out beta under independent adult denominator
spatial_generality.generality_rule: Do not claim a Palmer-wide positive-density-dependence mechanism if island-specific beta signs disagree or any leave-one-island-out adult-denominator beta is <=0.

semantics_checks: fraction of legacy chick-table rows with chicks > 2 * legacy pairs
fraction of independent-adult matched rows with chicks > 2 * adult pairs
fraction of pair denominators exactly matching between sources
median absolute and relative pair-count differences
interpretation_boundary: This audit is post-outcome and resolves measurement/statistical semantics; it is not a new confirmatory ecological test.
A positive pooled count-space effect does not establish an Allee effect, social facilitation or predation mechanism.
If island signs disagree, report spatial heterogeneity rather than a common Palmer small-group disadvantage.
The legacy ratio regression is not treated as a robustness gold standard because its denominator fails independent measurement-semantics checks.
Strong unstructured overdispersion sensitivity from the previously frozen v2 result remains part of the final claim boundary.
